methodology_note: FCF proxy is UNDERLYING PROFIT, NOT operating cash flow. For ORA/DMF retirement village operators, reported operating cash flow ($279.9m in 1H26) is inflated by resident occupation-right receipts, which are capital/financing inflows the company must continuously redeploy into new units. Underlying Profit is discounted at the cost of EQUITY (it is already after finance costs, so net debt is NOT subtracted again) with an exit-P/E cap tied to the 10yr realised range. UPDATE 2026-08-28: Underlying Profit is now built COMPONENT-WISE (development margin = deliveries x margin/unit; resale gains = resale volume x gain/resale; plus core operating earnings) rather than grown at a single rate. This was required because the H1-2026 result changed the two components in opposite directions and a single growth rate cannot express that.

provenance.note: Built on Opus, not the usual Fable tier, because Fable hit a rate limit in this session. The component UP build, the terminal-growth decomposition and the reconciliation bridge are the judgment-heavy parts and should be reviewed on the next full Fable pass.

inputs.share_count_basis: Shares on issue at 30 Jun 2026 (basic, in thousands: 243,483) per H1-2026 note 10. Up from 241,745 at FY25 and 242.361m used in the prior DCF; the increase is the dividend reinvestment plan (1,470,575 shares issued on the 26 Mar 2026 dividend), not an equity raise.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Management-stated net debt of $2,058m at 1H26 (presentation p35). Interest-bearing loans and borrowings $2,074.8m less cash $14.1m = $2,060.7m; the $2.7m difference is capitalised borrowing costs. Net debt ROSE from $1,960m at FY25 despite the deleveraging target, driven by $85.3m development outflow and $25m of AUD FX translation.
inputs.gearing_target: 30-40% band; company targets 33% and net debt below $1.9b by end-2027; target debt range REDUCED to $1.75b-$2.25b
inputs.nta_note: 1,441.33 CENTS per share at 1H26 = NZ$14.4133. The Metrics.csv NTAPerShare column is in cents; do not mis-scale.
inputs.notes: Model: Underlying Profit capitalized at cost of equity with an exit-P/E cap (ORA/DMF operator row of the dcf-methods routing table, matching the prior valuation). NOT an owner-FCF DCF: OCF is not free cash flow for this business model. Net debt is deliberately NOT subtracted from the capitalized value because Underlying Profit is already post-finance-cost.

historical_growth.note: The prior model's 18.96% 5yr UP CAGR anchor is now explicitly rejected as a forward driver. 1H26 UP FELL 3.0% year on year, and the historical CAGR was earned in a period when Summerset was scaling deliveries from ~350 to ~700 units a year. Management has now capped the build rate at 600-700, so the volume lever that produced that CAGR is closed. The base case implies a ~5.5% UP CAGR off FY2025's $234.2m.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported NZ IFRS profit rose 91.7% in 1H26 while Underlying Profit fell 3.0%. The entire IFRS increase is the fair-value movement of investment property (-$191.1m in the UP reconciliation vs -$85.6m in 1H25, +123.3%). This is IAS-40 revaluation noise, not earnings. The share price rose from $7.87 to $8.58 on the release, which is consistent with the market rewarding the IFRS headline. The valuation deliberately ignores it.

base.description: Build rate held at management's 600-700/yr cap: new sales converge from FY25's 805 (which drew down completed stock) to ~655. Development margin per unit recovers from 1H26's depressed $142k toward the $186k ex-Cambridge/Whangarei normalised level as the lightweight-design buildings clear, consistent with 20-25% guidance. Resale gains compound with the maturing installed base ($2.0b embedded value). Core operating earnings turn positive by Y3 on the $30-40m cost-out programme and occupancy ramp. Cost of equity 11%.

bull.description: NZ property recovers, resale velocity and ORA pricing lift, land bank optionality lets Summerset reaccelerate deliveries toward 850 (management explicitly retains this option), margins return to 25%+, Australia scales to three villages. Core operating earnings inflect strongly on operating leverage. Cost of equity 10%, exit P/E capped at 22x.

bear.description: Build rate settles at the bottom of the 600-700 band, development margin stays at the 1H26 20% rate as the adverse mix (serviced apartments -11%, memory care -2%) persists rather than reverting, NZ property stagnates, Australia execution slips, and core operating earnings stay negative. Cost of equity 12.5%, exit P/E 12.7x (10yr minimum).

entry_price.method: PV at the 15% hurdle of the five interim Underlying Profit years plus a terminal value REBUILT AT THE HURDLE RATE -- min(Gordon@15%, exit_pe_cap x UP5). Net debt is NOT subtracted: Underlying Profit is already post-finance-cost. The prior version built the terminal value at the 11% cost of equity and discounted it at 15%, which assumes an exit buyer accepting the CoE while the holder demands 15%. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Intrinsic value/share (NZD), base-case component build, across cost of equity (rows) and terminal growth (cols). Values plateau in the top-left because the 14.9x exit-P/E cap binds there.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Changed from 25/50/25 to 30/50/20. The build-rate cap is a management decision already taken, not a risk that may or may not occur, so the bull case now requires an active reacceleration rather than mere continuation - that is a higher bar than it was in June. The bear case correspondingly gained weight because the negative-margin mix (serviced apartments -11%, memory care -2%) is a disclosed fact about the current book, not a hypothetical.

bridge.item: Methodology: single growth rate on UP -> component build (deliveries x margin/unit + resales x gain/resale + core op)
bridge.note: Near-neutral by construction: holding FY2025 economics, the component model reproduces the prior answer. This isolates the driver change below as the real cause.

bridge.item: H1-2026 evidence: build rate capped at 600-700/yr, development margin compression to 20%, partly offset by improving core operating earnings and resale gains

reconciliation.price_move_note: The share price rose 9.0% from $7.87 to $8.58 on the 27-Aug release and now trades $8.49. The valuation fell. The divergence is the point of this update: the market moved on NZ IFRS profit +91.7%, which is fair-value revaluation, while Underlying Profit fell 3.0%.

nta_cross_check.note: Stock trades at 0.59x NTA of $14.41, a 41% discount, versus a 10yr median P/NTA of ~1.52x and a 10yr minimum of ~0.89x. The discount is wider than at any point in the ticker's history. But NTA is NOT a hard floor here: it is dominated by investment property carried at fair value under IAS 40, and that fair value embeds the same development margins and resale assumptions the operating result just called into question. NTA per share grew 11.5% year on year precisely because of the $191.1m revaluation that Underlying Profit strips out. Treating an asset value as a floor when the asset is marked to a model that assumes the cash flows you are doubting is circular. The base-case IV of $12.91 sits at 0.90x NTA, close to the historical minimum P/NTA, which is the more honest anchor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: At $8.49 Summerset trades on roughly 9x FY2026E Underlying Profit and 0.59x NTA. That is genuinely cheap against its own history. The base case of $12.91 implies a re-rate to ~14x on a slowly compounding earnings base, and the weighted $12.90 offers 52% upside. But the shape of the thesis changed with the H1-2026 result. Summerset's Underlying Profit is not an operating earnings stream: core operations lose money (-$9.4m in 1H26), and 100%+ of Underlying Profit comes from realised development margin and realised resale gains. Management has now capped the build rate at 600-700 homes a year, which caps the development leg, and the margin on that leg fell to 20% from 29%. What is left compounding is the resale book, which is the better business - it is asset-light, it grows with the installed base, and management estimates $2.0b of embedded value in it. The investment case is therefore narrower than it was: it is a bet on the resale annuity plus a multiple re-rate, with the development engine reframed from growth driver to maintenance capex.
valuation_philosophy.key_change: Build rate capped 600-700/yr and development margin compressed to 20%; UP now built component-wise; weights to 30/50/20; bull exit P/E 29x -> 22x. Weighted IV 16.81 -> 12.90.
valuation_philosophy.is_the_prior_number_defensible: No. The prior $16.81 was too high. It grew Underlying Profit at 16% in year 1 off a 18.96% 5yr CAGR anchor, when the corrected 3yr CAGR was already ~11% and the prior model's own growth_divergence_warning said the 16% sat above trend. 1H26 then delivered -3.0%. The error was not arithmetic; it was extrapolating a CAGR earned by scaling deliveries into a period when management has stopped scaling deliveries.

sanity_check.diagnosis: Base-case implied exit multiple of 14.1x P/UP sits essentially on the 10yr median of 14.9x and inside the realised 12.7-29.0x range; implied P/NTA of 0.90x sits at the 10yr minimum. Neither requires the market to pay more than it has paid before. Terminal value is 70% of base equity value, which is high but normal for a capitalization model and is constrained by the exit-P/E cap in the aggressive corner of the sensitivity grid. No self-justification of a gap to market price was needed: the model moved DOWN toward the price rather than the price being declared wrong.
